teaser: An augmented PDF viewer in the browser: PDF.js draws the page, one more layer adds provenance and graph, and the PDF only carries clues.
core_idea: A browser viewer that renders any PDF and adds an augmented layer of provenance, graph, definitions and comments is feasible on open source: PDF.js, Apache-licensed and active, draws pages in layers and reads attachments, metadata, links and a fingerprint; the layer need not live in the PDF, which only carries clues tried in order, from an embedded file to a printed QR code; Hypothesis, e-invoices and C2PA are precedents; the hard parts are the interface, anchors that survive, and a signed layer, never JavaScript inside the PDF.
